title: Lessons with Tio: counting, keeping time, fingering
summary: Tio made him keep his foot going to count note values; he demonstrated difficult fingerings on his own clarinet. Simeon also comments on drummers pushing a soloist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: And that's about all that you've got on. Can you tell us some more about your lessons with Teo and your counting and rhythm?

When I first started, Teo impressed, always impressed it. You had to keep your foot. For whole notes, four beats. For a half note, two beats. A quarter note, one beat. But I always had to keep that foot going while I was playing my exercises. I had to keep the foot going to keep it on time. And then later on after I started playing with the little bands around Chicago, then the drums. Then you've got the tempo and the beat from the drums. I mean the drums inspire you to play, you know. A drummer should push a soloist. I mean you should give them that drive. And he's very important. And a dance man, jazz man.
Can you tell us a little more about Teo? Did he play clarinet with you at the lessons? Did he have his instrument there to demonstrate, or did he do all of them?
Well, he always had his clarinet alongside him. And there were certain passages that I couldn't finger. He showed me how to finger that particular passage. He showed me which keys to press down.
